techniques.title: Eliminate a variable using the given constraint before differentiating
Differentiate the resulting single-variable expression and set dy/dx = 0
Use the second derivative to justify a maximum or minimum (rather than assuming)
Multiply two separate binomial expansions together, truncating at the required power
Prove the arithmetic series sum formula by writing the series forwards and backwards and adding
Find the area under a parametric curve using Area = integral of y (dx/dt) dt
Substitute u = e^(kt) to turn an equation with a repeated exponential term into a quadratic
Use the substitution x = a sin^2(theta) to integrate expressions of the form sqrt(x(a-x))
Factorise a difference of two squares and check all integer factor pairs
Find the perimeter of a region bounded by arcs of two intersecting circles
Take logs of both sides before differentiating implicitly (for y = f(x)^g(x) type functions)
Take logs of both sides of y = k*x^n to get a linear graph of log(y) against log(x)
Use the subtraction law of logs to turn a sum of logs of ratios into a telescoping sum
Solve a modulus equation by splitting into cases
Sum a periodic sequence using complete repeating blocks
Combine the discriminant with a domain-endpoint check to find a range of k for a line meeting a restricted curve
Check candidate roots of a converted log equation against the domain of the logarithms
Find the long-run limit of an exponential model to evaluate it
Adjust the sum-to-infinity formula for a geometric series that starts at n=2 (or later) instead of n=1
Use a substitution like u = 1 + sqrt(x) to clear a square root from the denominator before integrating

question_types.title: Optimise a 3D shape under a constraint
question_types.definition: A solid or container with a fixed volume: show a surface-area formula in one variable, then use calculus to find and justify the optimum.

question_types.title: Maximise a quantity given by a model
question_types.definition: A context model (speed, growth rate, bounce height) whose maximum is found by differentiating the model itself, often needing a product/chain rule and interpretation.

question_types.title: Stationary points, nature & concavity
question_types.definition: Differentiate a given curve (once or twice) to find or verify stationary points, classify them, or find where the curve is concave/convex or has an inflection.

question_types.title: Differentiate to a given form, then use it
question_types.definition: Quotient/product/chain rule on a single function to reach a printed form, often followed by increasing/decreasing or a condition on a constant.

question_types.title: Differentiation from first principles
question_types.definition: Prove a derivative (polynomial or sin/cos) from the gradient of a chord and a limit as h -> 0.

question_types.title: Implicit differentiation with tangents/normals
question_types.definition: Find dy/dx for an implicitly defined curve (or x = f(y)), then use it for a normal, tangent, extreme point or inflection.

question_types.title: Turning point located by iteration
question_types.definition: Differentiate, set the derivative to zero, rearrange into x = g(x), then iterate and/or confirm the root with a sign change.

question_types.title: Locate a root and apply Newton-Raphson/cobweb
question_types.definition: Show a root lies in an interval by sign change, then apply Newton-Raphson or judge an iteration from a cobweb diagram.

question_types.title: Trapezium rule estimate
question_types.definition: Apply the trapezium rule to a table of values, then reuse, judge or compare the estimate (sometimes with the exact integral).

question_types.title: Exponential model in context
question_types.definition: Find the constants of an exponential model from data, then predict, differentiate for a rate, compare two models or evaluate/adapt the model.

question_types.title: Straight-line log graph model
question_types.definition: A straight-line graph of log y against x or log x is used to find the constants in y = ab^x or y = kx^n, then interpret or use the model.

question_types.title: Log laws and log equations
question_types.definition: Manipulate or solve equations using the laws of logarithms, usually removing logs and rejecting invalid roots.

question_types.title: Exponential and index equations
question_types.definition: Solve an equation with the unknown in the power (by a common base, logs, or a hidden quadratic), sometimes with a sketch of y = a^x.

question_types.title: Find a curve from its gradient function
question_types.definition: Integrate powers of x (indefinite), using a point, turning point or factor to find the constant(s) of integration.

question_types.title: Area bounded by a polynomial curve (and a line)
question_types.definition: Algebraic integration of polynomial/fractional powers to find an exact area bounded by a curve, the axis and/or a tangent or straight line.

question_types.title: Definite integrals of standard forms
question_types.definition: A short definite integral of a standard form (1/(ax + b), (ax + b)^-2, x^(1/2)), sometimes written as the limit of a sum, simplified exactly.

question_types.title: Integration by parts (exact answer)
question_types.definition: An exact definite integral or area needing integration by parts (possibly twice or combined with a normal).

question_types.title: Integration by a given substitution
question_types.definition: Use a given substitution (including trigonometric) to transform and evaluate an integral exactly, changing the limits.

question_types.title: Partial fractions, then integrate or differentiate
question_types.definition: Express a rational function in partial fractions (or divide an improper fraction), then integrate exactly or differentiate.

question_types.title: Area under a parametric curve
question_types.definition: Set up the integral of y(dx/dt) dt for a parametric region, simplify with trig identities and evaluate exactly.

question_types.title: Form and solve a differential equation from a description
question_types.definition: A worded rate statement (proportional to..., constant volume rate, flow in/out) is turned into a DE, sometimes via connected rates, then solved and interpreted.

question_types.title: Solve a given separable differential equation
question_types.definition: The DE is given; separate variables (possibly after partial fractions or a substitution), use conditions, rearrange and interpret.

question_types.title: Binomial expansion, validity & approximation
question_types.definition: Expand (a + bx)^n, state validity and use it to approximate a value, sometimes combined with partial fractions or integration.

question_types.title: Vector lengths, angles and shapes
question_types.definition: Use magnitudes of vectors (Pythagoras in 3D) for lengths, distances, areas or angles, often to classify or measure a shape.

question_types.title: Parallel vectors, collinearity and ratios
question_types.definition: Use scalar multiples to show parallel/collinear results or to locate a point dividing a line in a ratio.

question_types.title: Proof by contradiction
question_types.definition: Prove a statement by assuming its negation (parity, factor pairs, trig inequality) and reaching a contradiction.

question_types.title: Algebraic proof by cases / counterexample
question_types.definition: Prove a number property by writing n in general forms (2k, 2k+1, 3k+r) and checking every case, or disprove a claim with a counterexample.

question_types.title: Circle meets a line: tangency and intersections
question_types.definition: Find a circle's centre/radius or equation, then substitute a line and use the discriminant (or the tangent-radius property) for tangents or two intersections.

question_types.title: Circle centre/radius with distances
question_types.definition: Complete the square for the centre and radius, then use distances from the centre (furthest point, two circles intersecting).

question_types.title: Small angle approximations
question_types.definition: Replace sin, cos and tan by their small-angle approximations to estimate a value, a root or an expression.

question_types.title: Arcs, sectors and composite circular regions
question_types.definition: Use radian arc-length and sector-area formulae (with triangles/segments) to find angles, lengths, areas or perimeters.

question_types.title: Trig identity, then solve an equation
question_types.definition: Prove or use an identity (double/compound angle, reciprocal, Pythagorean) and then solve a related trig equation in an interval.

question_types.title: Harmonic form and trig models in context
question_types.definition: Write a cos x + b sin x as R cos(x +- alpha) and/or use a sinusoidal model to find maximum/minimum values and the times they occur.

question_types.title: Parametric differentiation and tangents
question_types.definition: Find dy/dx parametrically and use it for a tangent or gradient at a point (sometimes after converting to Cartesian form).

question_types.title: Parametric to Cartesian, with intersections
question_types.definition: Convert parametric equations to Cartesian form (usually by a trig identity), then use the parameter range and/or find intersections or a range of k.

question_types.title: Factor theorem: find the constant
question_types.definition: Given a linear factor of a polynomial with an unknown coefficient, set f(a) = 0 and solve for the constant.

question_types.title: Factorise a polynomial and solve
question_types.definition: Use a known root/factor to factorise a cubic, then solve exactly, find intersections, or count real roots of a related equation.

question_types.title: Quadratic and cubic graphs from features
question_types.definition: Complete the square or use roots/turning points to sketch a quadratic or cubic, read off features, or define a region with inequalities.

question_types.title: Linear and quadratic models in context
question_types.definition: Fit a linear or quadratic model to a context (trajectory, cost, growth) from given conditions, then use it, evaluate it or state a limitation.

question_types.title: Composite and inverse functions
question_types.definition: Evaluate or form composite functions, find inverses with their domains, and state ranges.

question_types.title: Modulus graphs and transformations
question_types.definition: Work with y = a|x - b| + c or |f(x)|: find the vertex, solve modulus equations/inequalities, find k for intersections, or map points under transformations.

question_types.title: Arithmetic and geometric sequences in context
question_types.definition: Use nth-term and sum formulae for an AP or GP (often a savings, speed, profit or race context), including forming and solving a quadratic in n.

question_types.title: Geometric series with unknowns
question_types.definition: Terms or sums of a GP are given in terms of an unknown; form and solve an equation (ratio property or sum formula), then use S_infinity.

question_types.title: Sums in sigma notation
question_types.definition: Evaluate a sigma-notation sum by splitting into AP/GP parts, adjusting the starting index, or telescoping.

question_types.title: Recurrence relations and periodic sequences
question_types.definition: Generate terms from u_(n+1) = f(u_n), find an unknown constant, and/or sum a periodic sequence.

question_types.title: Summary statistics, coding & the large data set
question_types.definition: Find the mean and standard deviation from Σx and Σx² (sometimes coded), then interpret, compare or choose measures, often with sampling, data-cleaning or large-data-set context.

question_types.title: Box plots, outliers & percentiles
question_types.definition: Complete or read a box plot, find outlier limits using a given rule, and link the data to the large data set or to a normal percentile range.

question_types.title: Regression line interpretation & PMCC test
question_types.definition: Interpret a scatter diagram or regression line in context and test ρ = 0 against a one- or two-tailed alternative using a critical value or p-value.

question_types.title: Log-coded regression to y = ax^n or y = kb^x
question_types.definition: Data coded with logarithms give a linear regression line; convert it back to a power or exponential model and find the constants, often with a correlation test too.

question_types.title: Venn diagram with unknown probabilities
question_types.definition: Use a Venn diagram of three or four events with unknown regions, and use independence, conditional probabilities and total probability = 1 to find the unknowns and further probabilities.

question_types.title: Tree diagram & conditional probability
question_types.definition: Build or complete a tree diagram for successive selections, find combined probabilities, and then a 'given that' probability.

question_types.title: Two-way table probabilities
question_types.definition: Read probabilities from a frequency table, extend it with percentages, and find union, intersection, complement and conditional probabilities.

question_types.title: Discrete distribution with an unknown constant
question_types.definition: A probability function or table has an unknown constant found from Σp = 1 (often via series, logs or algebra), then used for probabilities, including for two independent observations or linked to a Pure condition.

question_types.title: Evaluate a probability model against data
question_types.definition: Propose a uniform or binomial model for a large-data-set variable, calculate probabilities or expected frequencies with it, compare them with observed data and suggest refinements.

question_types.title: Binomial probabilities in context
question_types.definition: State the conditions for a binomial model, find exact and cumulative probabilities, possibly in two stages or using a normal approximation for large n.

question_types.title: Binomial hypothesis test with critical region
question_types.definition: State hypotheses for p, find a one- or two-tailed critical region, give the actual significance level and draw a conclusion from an observed value.

question_types.title: Normal distribution: probabilities & unknown parameters
question_types.definition: Find normal probabilities and use inverse normal z-values to find an unknown value, mean or standard deviation (sometimes solving simultaneous equations), possibly followed by a follow-on binomial or test part.

question_types.title: Normal distribution with conditional probability
question_types.definition: Find normal probabilities and then conditional probabilities such as P(X > a | X > b), often critiquing or refining the model, and often ending with a test for the mean.

question_types.title: Hypothesis test for a normal mean
question_types.definition: Test μ using the sample mean distribution N(μ, σ²/n), including one- or two-tailed tests and p-values, as the main part of the question.

question_types.title: Histogram with competing distribution models
question_types.definition: Estimate probabilities from a histogram (area = frequency), then compare a normal model and a fitted curve model (using integration) against the data.

question_types.title: Constant acceleration in a straight line
question_types.definition: Use suvat formulae for motion in one dimension, sometimes combined with a simple F = ma to find a driving force.

question_types.title: Speed-time / velocity-time graph problem
question_types.definition: Use the gradient and area of a piecewise-linear speed-time graph to find accelerations, distances and an unknown speed.

question_types.title: Constant acceleration with i-j vectors
question_types.definition: Use vector suvat (v = u + at, r = ut + ½at²) to find velocities, positions, distances, speeds, bearings or the time when motion is parallel to a given vector.

question_types.title: Vector forces and F = ma
question_types.definition: Add force vectors, use the direction of the resultant to form an equation, then apply F = ma and vector suvat.

question_types.title: Variable acceleration using vector calculus
question_types.definition: Differentiate or integrate r, v or a given as functions of t in i-j form, using initial conditions, speed, direction or perpendicular/parallel conditions.

question_types.title: Projectile from ground: range, height & path
question_types.definition: A projectile launched from level ground: show results linking U and α, find the range and greatest height or the equation of the path, and comment on modelling.

question_types.title: Projectile passing through a given point or colliding
question_types.definition: Use horizontal and vertical motion to eliminate time for a projectile that passes through a target point (or meets another projectile), usually leading to an equation in tan α.

question_types.title: Projectile from a height (cliff)
question_types.definition: A projectile launched from above the ground lands at a known horizontal distance; find the time, height, speed or greatest height using signed vertical displacement.

question_types.title: Particle on a rough horizontal plane
question_types.definition: Resolve forces (often a force at an angle) to find the normal reaction, use F = μR and F = ma, and then deceleration or stopping distance once the force is removed.

question_types.title: Particle on a rough inclined plane
question_types.definition: Resolve parallel and perpendicular to an inclined plane for equilibrium or motion, find the friction or μ, and decide whether the particle moves.

question_types.title: Connected particles over a pulley
question_types.definition: Write equations of motion for two particles joined by a string over a pulley (one on a rough plane), find the tension and acceleration, then look at what happens after the string goes slack or the particle hits the ground.

question_types.title: Rod or ladder in limiting equilibrium
question_types.definition: A rod on rough ground resting against a wall, peg, rail or drum (or held by a string): take moments, resolve, and use F = μR to find reactions, μ or the resultant force.

question_types.title: Horizontal beam held by rope against a wall
question_types.definition: A horizontal plank hinged or pressed against a wall and supported by an inclined rope with a load: find the tension by moments, the wall reaction and its direction, and limits on where the load can go.

skill_groups.title: Data Presentation, Outliers & the Large Data Set

skills.title: Rewrite expressions using index laws
skills.description: Turn roots, reciprocals and products into powers of x (e.g. 1/sqrt(x) = x^(-1/2)) or into a common base before differentiating, integrating or solving.

skills.title: Combine and simplify algebraic fractions
skills.description: Put fractions over a common denominator, multiply through by denominators and cancel common factors.

skills.title: Rearrange a formula to change its subject
skills.description: Collect the terms containing the required letter, factorise it out and divide, keeping the order of operations correct.

skills.title: Solve two linear simultaneous equations
skills.description: Form two equations from two pieces of information and solve them together to find two unknown constants.

skills.title: Simplify surds and rationalise denominators
skills.description: Write answers as simplified surds (e.g. 3sqrt(2)) and rationalise denominators where required.

skills.title: Solve an equation of the form x^n = k
skills.description: Isolate the power (e.g. r^3 = 1050, p^7 = 1.5625, r^(3/2) = 118) and take the appropriate root or power.

skills.title: Substitute to find intersections
skills.description: Substitute one equation into another (a line into a curve or circle, or parametric x(t), y(t) into a Cartesian equation) to get a single equation to solve.

skills.title: Solve a quadratic equation
skills.description: Solve a three-term quadratic by factorising, the quadratic formula or completing the square, giving exact roots when asked.

skills.title: Complete the square
skills.description: Write ax^2 + bx + c as a(x + p)^2 + q to read off turning points, show an expression is always positive, or find a circle centre.

skills.title: Use the discriminant b^2 - 4ac
skills.description: Choose the right condition (> 0 two roots, = 0 tangent/repeated root, < 0 no real roots) and solve for the unknown constant.

skills.title: Solve a quadratic (or other) inequality
skills.description: Find the critical values, then use a sketch or sign analysis to choose the inside or outside region.

skills.title: Spot and solve a quadratic in disguise
skills.description: Recognise a quadratic in e^x, 2^x, r^5, y^2 or similar, substitute u for it, solve, then convert back and reject impossible values.

skills.title: Use the factor theorem
skills.description: If (x - a) is a factor then f(a) = 0: substitute to find an unknown constant or to confirm a factor.

skills.title: Factorise a cubic using a known factor
skills.description: Divide (by long division or inspection) by a known linear factor to get a quadratic factor, then solve or analyse it.

skills.title: Find a quadratic or cubic from its features
skills.description: Use roots, repeated roots, a turning point, an intercept or given points (from a graph or a context) to find the equation, e.g. y = ax(x - 6)^2, H = ax^2 + bx + c.

skills.title: Apply graph transformations
skills.description: Map points or curves under y = af(x), f(x + a), f(ax), -f(x), f(-x) and combinations, or describe a transformation fully.

skills.title: Sketch a curve showing key features
skills.description: Draw the correct shape (including exponential, modulus and polynomial curves) and label intercepts, turning points, asymptotes and end behaviour.

skills.title: Sketch modulus graphs and find the vertex
skills.description: Sketch y = a|x - b| + c or y = |f(x)| and read off the vertex and intercepts.

skills.title: Solve modulus equations and inequalities
skills.description: Remove the modulus by taking the relevant branch(es) (or cases), solve, and check each solution against the graph.

skills.title: Find the values of k for which a line meets a graph
skills.description: Use the graph to find critical cases (through a vertex or endpoint, parallel to a branch, tangent) and combine them into a range of k.

skills.title: Use a graph to justify the number of roots
skills.description: Rearrange an equation into two graphs you can sketch and count the intersections to explain how many roots there are.

skills.title: Evaluate and form composite functions
skills.description: Work out fg(x) by applying g first and then f (choosing the right branch of a piecewise function); evaluate at a value or simplify fully.

skills.title: Find and use inverse functions
skills.description: Swap x and y and rearrange to find f^(-1)(x), state its domain from the range of f, and know when an inverse exists (one-one).

skills.title: State domains and ranges
skills.description: Use the graph, turning point or asymptote of a function to state its range (or the domain of its inverse) with correct notation.

skills.title: Find the equation of a straight line
skills.description: Use y - y1 = m(x - x1) with a gradient and a point, and give the answer in the form asked for.

skills.title: Use perpendicular gradients
skills.description: A perpendicular line (a normal, or a radius meeting a tangent) has gradient equal to the negative reciprocal: m1 x m2 = -1.

skills.title: Find distances between points
skills.description: Use Pythagoras on the coordinate differences to find a length or a distance between centres.

skills.title: Find a circle's centre and radius (or write its equation)
skills.description: Complete the square on x and y to get (x - a)^2 + (y - b)^2 = r^2 and read off the centre and radius, or write the equation from a known centre and radius.

skills.title: Solve problems with two circles or distances to a circle
skills.description: Use the distance between centres (and the radii) to decide how circles intersect, or find the furthest/nearest point.

skills.title: Use the nth term of an arithmetic sequence
skills.description: Use u_n = a + (n - 1)d to find a term, the common difference or the number of terms.

skills.title: Sum an arithmetic series
skills.description: Use S_n = n/2[2a + (n - 1)d] (or n/2(a + l)), often setting it equal to a total to form a quadratic in n.

skills.title: Use the nth term of a geometric sequence
skills.description: Use u_n = ar^(n - 1) to find a term or the common ratio, including percentage-growth contexts.

skills.title: Sum a finite geometric series
skills.description: Use S_n = a(1 - r^n)/(1 - r) with the correct first term and number of terms.

skills.title: Use the sum to infinity and the convergence condition
skills.description: A geometric series converges only if |r| < 1; then S_infinity = a/(1 - r).

skills.title: Form an equation using the common ratio
skills.description: For three consecutive terms, set term2/term1 = term3/term2 and simplify to an equation in the unknown.

skills.title: Prove the arithmetic or geometric series formula
skills.description: Write S_n forwards and backwards and add (arithmetic), or multiply by r and subtract (geometric).

skills.title: Generate terms from a recurrence relation
skills.description: Substitute repeatedly into u_(n+1) = f(u_n) to find terms, often in terms of an unknown constant, and form an equation.

skills.title: Sum a periodic sequence
skills.description: Identify the repeating block and its order, then sum complete blocks plus any leftover terms.

skills.title: Evaluate sums in sigma notation
skills.description: Split a sigma sum into standard parts, adjust for a starting index other than 1, or spot a telescoping pattern.

skills.title: Take out a factor before expanding (a + bx)^n
skills.description: Rewrite (a + bx)^n as a^n(1 + bx/a)^n before using the expansion.

skills.title: State the range of validity of an expansion
skills.description: The expansion of (1 + ax)^n is valid for |ax| < 1; use this to decide which x values may be substituted.
skills.formula_booklet_note: partly: only the condition |x|<1 for (1+x)^n; rewriting (a+bx)^n is not given

skills.title: Use an expansion to approximate a value
skills.description: Choose a suitable x, substitute into both the expression and the expansion, and comment on accuracy or over/underestimate.

skills.title: Multiply series and truncate at a power
skills.description: Multiply two expansions (or an expansion by a polynomial) keeping only terms up to the required power.

skills.title: Write out binomial expansion terms
skills.description: Expand (1 + ax)^n for fractional or negative n (1 + nx + n(n-1)/2! (ax)^2 + ...), or find a coefficient in (a + bx)^n with nCr, bracketing (ax)^k correctly.
skills.formula_booklet_note: (a+b)^n for n in N, and (1+x)^n for |x|<1

skills.title: Apply the laws of logarithms
skills.description: Use the addition, subtraction and power laws (and log_a a = 1) to combine or split logarithms.
skills.formula_booklet_note: partly: only change of base log_a x = log_b x / log_b a and e^(x ln a) = a^x; the other log laws are not given

skills.title: Solve exponential equations using logarithms
skills.description: Isolate the exponential term (or set two exponential models equal), then take logs to bring the power down and solve.

skills.title: Convert a log equation into an equation without logs
skills.description: Combine into a single log, then use log_a x = b <=> x = a^b (or e^(ln x) = x) to remove the logs.

skills.title: Find the constants in an exponential model
skills.description: Substitute given data (usually t = 0 first) into V = Ae^(kt), V = Ap^t or theta = A - Be^(-kt) and solve for the constants.

skills.title: Use a straight-line log graph to find model constants
skills.description: Take logs of y = ab^x or y = kx^n to get a straight line; match the gradient and intercept to find the constants.

skills.title: Differentiate a model to find a rate of change
skills.description: Differentiate the model with respect to time and substitute a value, or use a given rate to find a constant.

skills.title: Translate a context into a mathematical model
skills.description: Turn a worded description into an equation: linear cost, quadratic path, arithmetic/geometric growth, or a proportional rate.

skills.title: Use a model to make a prediction
skills.description: Substitute a value into a model (or solve for the input), including an optimum found by calculus, and answer in context with units.

skills.title: Evaluate a model against real data
skills.description: Compare a model prediction with a given true value and conclude whether the model is reliable, with a reason.

skills.title: Interpret constants in a model
skills.description: Explain what a constant means in context (initial value, growth factor per year, cost per item).

skills.title: State a limitation of a model
skills.description: Give a specific reason the model may break down (negative values, unrealistic assumptions, outside the data range).

skills.title: Find the long-term (limiting) value of a model
skills.description: Let t tend to infinity (e^(-kt) -> 0) or set the rate to zero to find a limiting value, and interpret it.

skills.title: Find arc lengths (radians)
skills.description: Use s = r theta with theta in radians, including perimeters of sectors and composite shapes.

skills.title: Find sector areas (radians)
skills.description: Use A = (1/2) r^2 theta with theta in radians.

skills.title: Find areas and perimeters of composite circular regions
skills.description: Build a region from sectors, triangles and segments (e.g. overlapping circles, logos), adding and subtracting pieces.

skills.title: Use sine rule, cosine rule and (1/2)ab sin C
skills.description: Find sides, angles or areas of non-right-angled triangles.

skills.title: Use exact trig values
skills.description: Use exact values of sin, cos and tan at 0, pi/6, pi/4, pi/3, pi/2 (and related angles) to keep answers exact.

skills.title: Use small angle approximations
skills.description: Replace sin x ~ x, tan x ~ x and cos x ~ 1 - x^2/2 (x in radians, watch the argument, e.g. cos 3x ~ 1 - 9x^2/2).
skills.formula_booklet_note: sin x ~ x, cos x ~ 1 - x^2/2, tan x ~ x (radians)

skills.title: Use sec, cosec and cot
skills.description: Rewrite sec, cosec and cot as 1/cos, 1/sin and cos/sin (and tan as sin/cos) to simplify.

skills.title: Use Pythagorean identities
skills.description: Use sin^2 + cos^2 = 1, 1 + tan^2 = sec^2 and 1 + cot^2 = cosec^2 to change the form of an expression.

skills.title: Use double angle formulae
skills.description: Use sin 2A = 2 sin A cos A and the three forms of cos 2A, choosing the form that simplifies the expression.

skills.title: Use compound angle formulae
skills.description: Expand sin(A +- B), cos(A +- B), tan(A +- B), e.g. to find cos 3A or to rewrite a shifted trig function.

skills.title: Prove a trigonometric identity
skills.description: Start from one side, convert to sin and cos, use identities and algebra step by step until you reach the other side.

skills.title: Write a cos x + b sin x as R cos(x +- alpha) or R sin(x +- alpha)
skills.description: Find R = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) and alpha from tan alpha, matching the signs to the required form.

skills.title: Solve a trig equation in a given interval
skills.description: Find the principal value, then use the symmetry/period of the graph to list every solution in the interval (degrees or radians).

skills.title: Solve trig equations with a transformed argument
skills.description: For sin(2x + 30) = k etc., adjust the interval for the new argument, solve, then undo the transformation.

skills.title: Solve a quadratic in a trig function
skills.description: Use identities to get a quadratic in one trig function, solve it, and reject values outside [-1, 1].

skills.title: Factorise rather than divide to avoid losing solutions
skills.description: When a common factor such as sin x or sin 2x appears, factorise it out and solve each factor, instead of cancelling it.

skills.title: Use a trig model to find maximum, minimum and times
skills.description: Use the maximum/minimum of sin or cos (+-1, or R for harmonic form) to find extreme values and the times they occur in context.

skills.title: Find the parameters of a trig model
skills.description: Use the maximum, minimum, period and starting value to find the constants in a sinusoidal model.

skills.title: Differentiate polynomials
skills.description: Use d/dx(x^n) = nx^(n-1) term by term on polynomials.

skills.title: Differentiate negative and fractional powers
skills.description: Rewrite roots and reciprocals as powers, then use nx^(n-1) carefully with negative and fractional indices.

skills.title: Differentiate exponentials and logarithms
skills.description: Use d/dx(e^(kx)) = ke^(kx) and d/dx(ln x) = 1/x (and ln(f(x)) -> f'(x)/f(x)).

skills.title: Differentiate trig functions
skills.description: Differentiate sin(kx), cos(kx), tan(kx) and the reciprocal trig functions, including with the chain rule.
skills.formula_booklet_note: partly: only tan kx, sec kx, cot kx, cosec kx; sin and cos are not given

skills.title: Find the second derivative
skills.description: Differentiate the first derivative again (including quotient-rule second derivatives).

skills.title: Differentiate from first principles
skills.description: Write the gradient of the chord (f(x + h) - f(x))/h, simplify, and take the limit as h -> 0 with correct notation.

skills.title: Differentiate using the chain rule
skills.description: Differentiate a function of a function: d/dx f(g(x)) = f'(g(x)) g'(x), e.g. (3 + 7e^(-0.25t))^(-1).

skills.title: Differentiate using the product rule
skills.description: Use d/dx(uv) = u v' + v u' for products such as x ln x or e^(-2x)(x^2 - 2).

skills.title: Differentiate using the quotient rule
skills.description: Use d/dx(u/v) = (v u' - u v')/v^2, then simplify the numerator.

skills.title: Simplify a derivative to a given form
skills.description: Factorise and cancel common factors (e.g. e^(-2x), (x + 1)) so the derivative matches the printed form exactly.

skills.title: Differentiate implicitly
skills.description: Differentiate each term with respect to x, using y^n -> ny^(n-1) dy/dx and the product rule on xy terms, then make dy/dx the subject.

skills.title: Differentiate parametric equations
skills.description: Use dy/dx = (dy/dt)/(dx/dt), then substitute the parameter value for the point.

skills.title: Find the parameter value at a given point
skills.description: Solve x(t) = a or y(t) = b (checking the other coordinate) to find the parameter at a point, then use it.

skills.title: Link rates of change with the chain rule
skills.description: Combine rates such as dV/dt = (dV/dr)(dr/dt) or dh/dt = (dh/dV)(dV/dt) using a volume formula.

skills.title: Find the equation of a tangent
skills.description: Differentiate, substitute the x-coordinate for the gradient, and use y - y1 = m(x - x1).

skills.title: Find the equation of a normal
skills.description: Find the tangent gradient, take the negative reciprocal, and use the point to write the normal.

skills.title: Use gradient conditions (horizontal/vertical tangents, equal gradients)
skills.description: Interpret dy/dx = 0, dy/dx undefined, or f'(x) = g'(x) geometrically to set up the equation to solve.

skills.title: Set the derivative equal to zero and solve
skills.description: Stationary points occur where dy/dx = 0: set the derivative to zero, solve, and find the coordinates.

skills.title: Verify a stationary point at a given x
skills.description: Substitute the given x into dy/dx, show it equals 0 and make a conclusion.

skills.title: Determine the nature of a stationary point
skills.description: Substitute into the second derivative (positive: minimum, negative: maximum) or check the gradient either side (needed for a stationary point of inflection); state the sign and conclude.

skills.title: Use the derivative to find increasing/decreasing intervals
skills.description: f is increasing where f'(x) > 0 and decreasing where f'(x) < 0; solve the inequality or prove the sign.

skills.title: Use concavity and points of inflection
skills.description: Concave where f''(x) <= 0, convex where f''(x) >= 0; at a point of inflection f''(x) changes sign.

skills.title: Eliminate a variable using a constraint
skills.description: Use the fixed quantity (e.g. volume) to express one variable in terms of the other and substitute into the quantity to be optimised.

skills.title: Use area and volume formulae for 3D shapes
skills.description: Write surface areas and volumes of prisms, cylinders, spheres/hemispheres and cuboids.
skills.formula_booklet_note: partly: only surface area of a sphere 4 pi r^2 and curved surface of a cone pi r l; volumes are not given

skills.title: Integrate powers of x
skills.description: Use the integral of x^n = x^(n+1)/(n+1) term by term, including negative and fractional powers after rewriting.

skills.title: Evaluate a definite integral
skills.description: Substitute the limits into the integrated expression and subtract (upper minus lower), simplifying exactly; recognise lim (delta x -> 0) of sum f(x) delta x as the integral of f(x).

skills.title: Find the constant of integration from a point
skills.description: After integrating, substitute a known point (or initial condition) to find c.

skills.title: Use standard integrals (e^(kx), 1/x, trig)
skills.description: Integrate e^(kx), 1/(ax + b), sin(kx), cos(kx) and sec^2(kx) directly, remembering the 1/k factor.
skills.formula_booklet_note: partly: only sec^2 kx, tan kx, cot kx, cosec kx, sec kx; e^(kx), 1/x, sin, cos are not given

skills.title: Integrate by reverse chain rule (recognition)
skills.description: Recognise integrands of the form f'(x)[f(x)]^n or (ax + b)^n and integrate by inspection.

skills.title: Find the area under a curve
skills.description: Integrate between the x-intercepts or given limits; where the curve is below the x-axis the integral is negative, so split at roots and use magnitudes.

skills.title: Find the area between a curve and a line
skills.description: Integrate (top - bottom), or combine the area under the curve with triangle/trapezium areas.

skills.title: Find the area under a parametric curve
skills.description: Use Area = integral of y (dx/dt) dt with the limits changed to parameter values.

skills.title: Integrate by parts
skills.description: Choose u (often ln x or a polynomial) and dv/dx, apply the formula (twice if needed) and simplify.
skills.formula_booklet_note: integral u dv/dx dx = uv - integral v du/dx dx

skills.title: Integrate by substitution
skills.description: Use the given substitution to rewrite the whole integral (including dx) in terms of the new variable, then integrate.

skills.title: Change the limits when substituting
skills.description: Convert x-limits into limits for the new variable (u or theta) so you never need to substitute back.

skills.title: Use trig identities to integrate
skills.description: Rewrite sin^2, cos^2 or products using double angle identities before integrating.

skills.title: Integrate partial fractions to logarithms
skills.description: Integrate A/(ax + b) to (A/a) ln|ax + b| for each fraction, then combine logs into a single exact form.

skills.title: Divide out an improper algebraic fraction
skills.description: When the numerator degree >= denominator degree, divide first to get a polynomial plus a proper fraction (e.g. 4 - 7/(2x + 3)).

skills.title: Split a fraction into partial fractions
skills.description: Write A/(ax + b) + B/(cx + d) (or with a repeated factor B/(ax + b)^2), multiply through, and find the constants by substitution or comparing coefficients.

skills.title: Form a differential equation from a description
skills.description: Translate "rate of change is proportional to..." into dy/dt = k(...) with the correct sign.

skills.title: Separate the variables and integrate
skills.description: Rearrange to f(y) dy = g(x) dx, integrate both sides and include one constant of integration.

skills.title: Use initial/boundary conditions to find constants
skills.description: Substitute given (t, y) values to find the constant of integration and any proportionality constant.

skills.title: Rearrange a DE solution into the required form
skills.description: Remove logs (exponentiate) and make the dependent variable the subject, e.g. V = A/(e^(-kt) + B) or h = A + Be^(-kt).

skills.title: Show a root lies in an interval (change of sign)
skills.description: Evaluate f at both ends, show a sign change, state f is continuous, and conclude; use a tight interval to confirm a root to given accuracy.

skills.title: Use an iteration formula
skills.description: Substitute repeatedly into x_(n+1) = g(x_n), giving values to the required accuracy.

skills.title: Draw cobweb/staircase diagrams and judge convergence
skills.description: Draw a cobweb or staircase from x_1 and decide whether (and to which root) the iteration converges.

skills.title: Apply the Newton-Raphson method
skills.description: Use x_(n+1) = x_n - f(x_n)/f'(x_n) and know when it fails (e.g. f'(x_n) = 0 at a stationary point).

skills.title: Rearrange an equation into a given iterative form
skills.description: Manipulate f(x) = 0 or f'(x) = 0 algebraically into x = g(x) exactly as printed.

skills.title: Estimate an integral with the trapezium rule
skills.description: Use (h/2)[y0 + yn + 2(y1 + ... + y(n-1))] with the correct strip width h.

skills.title: Judge or reuse a trapezium estimate
skills.description: Explain over/underestimates from the curve shape, comment on accuracy, or scale a previous estimate using log laws or constant factors.

skills.title: Convert parametric equations to Cartesian form
skills.description: Eliminate the parameter by rearranging or by using a trig identity (sin^2 + cos^2 = 1, cos 2t = 1 - 2 sin^2 t, sec^2 = 1 + tan^2).

skills.title: Use the parameter range to find domain restrictions and endpoints
skills.description: Use the allowed values of t to find the end points of the curve and the restricted x or y values.

skills.title: Find the vector between two points
skills.description: Use AB = OB - OA (or add vectors along a path) in i, j, k form.

skills.title: Find the magnitude of a vector
skills.description: Use |ai + bj + ck| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2 + c^2) for lengths and distances.

skills.title: Use parallel and collinear vectors
skills.description: Vectors are parallel if one is a scalar multiple of the other; collinear points share a parallel vector and a point.

skills.title: Use vector ratios to locate points and prove geometric results
skills.description: Write a position vector using a ratio or scalar lambda, compare coefficients of non-parallel vectors, and prove ratios or shapes.

skills.title: Prove by contradiction
skills.description: Assume the negation, reason algebraically (e.g. factorise and check every integer factor pair) to something impossible, and conclude the original statement.

skills.title: Prove results using general odd/even/multiple forms
skills.description: Represent numbers as 2k, 2k + 1, 3k + 1, etc., expand, and factor to show the required form.

skills.title: Prove an inequality or that an expression is always positive
skills.description: Complete the square (square >= 0), or manipulate an inequality carefully, reversing the sign when multiplying/dividing by a negative.

skills.title: Prove by exhaustion or disprove by counterexample
skills.description: Split into a complete set of cases (or check every value) and show the result in each; or disprove a claim with one specific counterexample.

skills.title: Present a full "show that" argument
skills.description: When the answer is printed, show every step (including key intermediate lines) with no errors, and finish at exactly the given result.

skills.title: Use a previous part ("hence")
skills.description: Spot how an earlier result (identity, factor, expansion, derivative) transforms the new problem, and use it explicitly.

skills.title: Reject solutions that are invalid
skills.description: Check each solution against the domain, the context or the original equation (log of a negative, negative length, |r| >= 1, outside the interval) and reject with a reason.

skills.title: Give exact (calculator-free) answers
skills.description: Keep surds, pi, e and ln in exact form and combine logs, when told to show working or give an exact answer.

skills.title: Write answers in set notation
skills.description: Express ranges of values using correct set notation, including unions and intersections of intervals.

skills.title: Give answers to the required accuracy and units
skills.description: Round only at the end to the stated accuracy (s.f., d.p., nearest minute/metre) and include units; convert time formats.

skills.title: Explain or justify with a reason and conclusion
skills.description: Give a clear mathematical reason plus a minimal conclusion when asked to explain, justify or give a reason.

skills.title: Name a sampling method
skills.description: Recognise opportunity, quota, systematic, stratified or simple random sampling from a description.

skills.title: Describe how to carry out a sampling method
skills.description: Explain step by step how to take a quota, stratified, systematic or random sample in context.

skills.title: Compare sampling methods and census
skills.description: Give an advantage or disadvantage of a sampling method, or of a census compared with a sample.

skills.title: Identify the sample and population
skills.description: Say exactly what the sample is and what population it could be used to make inferences about.

skills.title: Mean from Σx
skills.description: Calculate the mean from Σx and n, including estimates from grouped data.

skills.title: Standard deviation from Σx and Σx²
skills.description: Find the standard deviation using √(Σx²/n − x̄²) or √(Sxx/n).

skills.title: Coding and its effect on mean and SD
skills.description: Undo a linear coding such as y = x − 1010 to recover the mean, knowing that adding a constant leaves the standard deviation unchanged.

skills.title: Median, quartiles, range and IQR
skills.description: Read or calculate the median, quartiles, range and interquartile range, including by interpolation for grouped data.

skills.title: Choose mean/SD or median/IQR
skills.description: Decide which measures best describe the data, giving skew or outliers as the reason.

skills.title: Effect of adding or changing values
skills.description: Reason, without recalculating everything, how changing or adding data values affects the mean, median, quartiles or standard deviation.

skills.title: Compare distributions in context
skills.description: Compare the location and spread of two data sets and draw a conclusion in context.

skills.title: Histogram area represents frequency
skills.description: Use frequency density × class width to find frequencies and estimate probabilities from a histogram.

skills.title: Read and draw box plots
skills.description: Read values from a box plot, or complete one with whiskers and outliers marked correctly.

skills.title: Identify outliers using a given rule
skills.description: Apply a rule such as Q1 − 1.5×IQR or mean ± 3 SD to decide which values are outliers.

skills.title: Clean data
skills.description: Deal with missing values, errors and entries such as 'tr' (trace) before calculating statistics.

skills.title: Use knowledge of the large data set
skills.description: Use facts about the large data set (locations, the May–Oct months, variables, units, typical values) to explain or identify data.

skills.title: Describe correlation
skills.description: Describe correlation as positive, negative or none, and as strong or weak, from a scatter diagram or r.

skills.title: Suggest a reason for correlation
skills.description: Give a sensible reason in context for a correlation, remembering that correlation does not imply causation.

skills.title: Explanatory and response variables
skills.description: Identify the explanatory variable by explaining which variable affects the other.

skills.title: Interpret regression gradient and intercept
skills.description: Interpret the gradient as a rate of change per unit (with units) and the intercept in context.

skills.title: Interpolation and extrapolation
skills.description: Use a regression line to make predictions and explain why extrapolating outside the data range is unreliable.

skills.title: Judge whether a linear model fits
skills.description: Use a scatter diagram shape or the size of r to decide whether a linear model is suitable.

skills.title: Convert a log-coded line to y = ax^n or y = kb^x
skills.description: Substitute the log codings into the regression line and remove logs to find the constants of a power or exponential model.

skills.title: Complement and addition rules
skills.description: Use P(A') = 1 − P(A) and P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A ∩ B).

skills.title: Draw and label a tree diagram
skills.description: Draw a tree diagram with correct branches and probabilities for successive events.

skills.title: Multiply along and add between branches
skills.description: Find the probability of combined outcomes, such as 'at least one', by multiplying along branches and adding the paths you need.

skills.title: Find unknown Venn diagram regions
skills.description: Set up equations from given probabilities and total probability = 1 to find unknown regions.

skills.title: Probabilities from two-way tables
skills.description: Read joint, marginal and conditional probabilities from a two-way table.

skills.title: Conditional probability
skills.description: Use P(A | B) = P(A ∩ B) / P(B), choosing the right restricted denominator.
skills.formula_booklet_evidence: P(A∩B) = P(A)P(B|A) and the P(A|B) formula

skills.title: Use or test independence
skills.description: Use P(A ∩ B) = P(A)P(B) to find unknowns or to show whether two events are independent.

skills.title: Mutually exclusive events
skills.description: Recognise events that cannot happen together, for example non-overlapping regions on a Venn diagram.

skills.title: Describe events in set notation
skills.description: Read and write events using ∩, ∪ and complements, such as [A ∪ B]' ∩ C.

skills.title: Find a constant using Σp = 1
skills.description: Set the sum of all probabilities equal to 1 to find an unknown constant, using series, logs or algebra where needed.

skills.title: Discrete uniform distribution
skills.description: Write down a discrete uniform distribution and find probabilities from it.

skills.title: Probabilities from a distribution
skills.description: List the values that satisfy an inequality or condition and add their probabilities.

skills.title: Combine two independent observations
skills.description: List the cases for two independent observations (such as a sum or equality) and multiply and add their probabilities.

skills.title: Probability of the first success on trial n
skills.description: Use (1 − p)^(n−1) × p for the first success happening on the nth independent trial.

skills.title: Expected frequencies and expected income
skills.description: Multiply probabilities by the number of trials or by values (such as prices) to get expected counts or totals.

skills.title: State binomial conditions in context
skills.description: State in context that trials are independent, with a fixed number of trials and a constant probability of success.

skills.title: Binomial P(X = x)
skills.description: Find an exact binomial probability with your calculator or nCx p^x (1 − p)^(n−x).
skills.formula_booklet_evidence: Binomial P(X = x) in the discrete distributions table

skills.title: Binomial cumulative probabilities
skills.description: Turn phrases like 'more than' or 'fewer than' into P(X ≤ k) or 1 − P(X ≤ k) and evaluate them.

skills.title: Two-stage binomial problems
skills.description: Use a probability from one binomial model as p in a second binomial model, for example the number of boxes or days.

skills.title: Binomial expectation np
skills.description: Use np to estimate the expected number of successes.
skills.formula_booklet_evidence: mean np, variance np(1-p) in the table

skills.title: Normal probabilities on a calculator
skills.description: Find P(X > a) or P(a < X < b) for X ~ N(μ, σ²) using a calculator.

skills.title: Inverse normal
skills.description: Find the value of x for a given cumulative probability, or a percentile or interpercentile range.
skills.formula_booklet_evidence: Percentage points of the normal distribution table (p. 34)

skills.title: Standardise to find μ or σ
skills.description: Set (x − μ)/σ equal to the correct z-value, with the right sign, to find an unknown mean or standard deviation.
skills.formula_booklet_evidence: Z = (X - μ)/σ is not printed (only the sample-mean version)

skills.title: Find μ and σ simultaneously
skills.description: Form two standardised equations from two given probabilities and solve them simultaneously for μ and σ.

skills.title: Conditional normal probabilities
skills.description: Find probabilities such as P(X > a | X > b) by writing the intersection over the given condition.

skills.title: Normal approximation to binomial
skills.description: Approximate B(n, p) by N(np, np(1 − p)) when n is large and p is close to 0.5.

skills.title: Continuity correction
skills.description: Adjust the boundary by 0.5 when using a continuous normal distribution to approximate a discrete one.

skills.title: Shape, symmetry and inflection of the normal curve
skills.description: Use the symmetry of the normal curve and its points of inflection at μ ± σ.

skills.title: Judge whether a binomial or normal model is suitable
skills.description: Explain whether a binomial or normal model suits the data, for example because of skew, negative values, qualitative data or non-constant p.

skills.title: State hypotheses for a binomial test
skills.description: Write H0 and H1 in terms of the population proportion p, choosing a one- or two-tailed alternative.

skills.title: Binomial test using a probability
skills.description: Work out P(X ≤ x) or P(X ≥ x) under H0 and compare it with the significance level.

skills.title: Find a binomial critical region
skills.description: Find the critical region(s) using cumulative probabilities, with half the significance level in each tail for a two-tailed test.

skills.title: Actual significance level
skills.description: Add the probabilities of the critical region(s) to find the actual significance level of a test.

skills.title: State hypotheses for a correlation test
skills.description: Write H0: ρ = 0 and an H1 of ρ > 0, ρ < 0 or ρ ≠ 0.

skills.title: Compare r with a critical value or p-value
skills.description: Use the PMCC critical value table or a given p-value to decide whether r is significant.
skills.formula_booklet_evidence: Critical values for correlation coefficients table (p. 37)

skills.title: Calculate r on a calculator
skills.description: Enter paired data into your calculator to find the product moment correlation coefficient.

skills.title: State hypotheses for a normal mean test
skills.description: Write H0 and H1 in terms of the population mean μ.

skills.title: Distribution of the sample mean
skills.description: Use X̄ ~ N(μ, σ²/n) to find the probability of the observed sample mean under H0.

skills.title: Two-tailed tests and p-values
skills.description: Split the significance level between the two tails, or double the one-tail probability to get the p-value.

skills.title: Conclude a test in context
skills.description: State whether there is enough evidence to reject H0 and give the conclusion in the words of the question, without being too definite.

skills.title: Critique probability model assumptions
skills.description: Question assumptions such as fairness, independence or constant probability, and describe the likely effect of more realistic ones.

skills.title: Suggest a refinement to a statistical model
skills.description: Suggest a specific improvement to a model, such as using different months or locations or a non-uniform distribution.

skills.title: Exact sin and cos from a given tan
skills.description: Use a right-angled triangle to get exact sin α and cos α from a value such as tan α = 3/4.

skills.title: SI units and conversions
skills.description: Use the right SI units and convert, for example, km h⁻¹ to m s⁻¹.

skills.title: suvat in one dimension
skills.description: Choose and apply the right constant-acceleration formula for straight-line motion.

skills.title: Gradient and area of velocity-time graphs
skills.description: Use the gradient for acceleration and the area under the graph for distance, including to find an unknown speed.

skills.title: Sketch a velocity-time graph
skills.description: Sketch a velocity-time graph with the correct shape and explain the shape using the acceleration.

skills.title: suvat with i-j vectors
skills.description: Apply v = u + at and r = r0 + ut + ½at² to vectors, then equate components where needed.
skills.formula_booklet_evidence: only the straight-line scalar forms are printed

skills.title: Speed, direction and bearing from a velocity vector
skills.description: Find speed as the magnitude of velocity, and direction as an angle or three-figure bearing using trig.

skills.title: Parallel or perpendicular direction conditions
skills.description: Set a component to zero or a ratio of components equal to form an equation for t when motion is parallel or perpendicular to a given direction.

skills.title: Differentiate r or v with respect to t
skills.description: Differentiate each component to go from position to velocity to acceleration.

skills.title: Integrate a or v with respect to t
skills.description: Integrate each component, including a vector constant found from the given initial conditions.

skills.title: Solve a speed condition for t
skills.description: Set the magnitude of a t-dependent velocity equal to a given speed and solve the resulting equation for t.

skills.title: Resolve the projection velocity
skills.description: Split the initial velocity into horizontal U cos α and vertical U sin α components.

skills.title: Horizontal motion of a projectile
skills.description: Use constant horizontal speed, x = (U cos α)t.

skills.title: Vertical motion of a projectile
skills.description: Apply suvat vertically with acceleration −g, taking care with signed displacement below the start point.

skills.title: Eliminate t between the two motions
skills.description: Substitute t from the horizontal equation into the vertical equation, often giving a quadratic in tan α using sec² = 1 + tan².

skills.title: Greatest height
skills.description: Use a vertical velocity of zero at the top to find the greatest height.

skills.title: Time of flight and range
skills.description: Find when the projectile lands and how far it travels horizontally.

skills.title: Speed and direction during flight
skills.description: Combine the horizontal and vertical velocity components at a given time to find the speed and angle of motion.

skills.title: Equation of the path
skills.description: Derive y in terms of x for a projectile and use it to find range or height.

skills.title: Draw a force diagram
skills.description: Mark weight, normal reaction, tension, thrust and friction in the right directions.

skills.title: Resolve a force at an angle
skills.description: Split a pull or push at an angle into components, and see how it changes the normal reaction.

skills.title: Resolve forces on an inclined plane
skills.description: Resolve weight and other forces parallel and perpendicular to the slope, e.g. R = mg cos α.

skills.title: Form an F = ma equation
skills.description: Write resultant force = mass × acceleration in the direction of motion, with the correct signs.

skills.title: Equilibrium of a particle
skills.description: Resolve in two perpendicular directions and set each resultant to zero.

skills.title: Connected particles equations
skills.description: Write separate equations of motion (or one whole-system equation) for particles joined by a string over a smooth pulley, and solve for T and a.

skills.title: Resultant of force vectors
skills.description: Add forces given in i-j form, and use F = ma in vector form.

skills.title: Magnitude and direction of a resultant force
skills.description: Use Pythagoras and tan on the perpendicular components to find the size and direction of a resultant or contact force.

skills.title: Weight and the value of g
skills.description: Use W = mg with the stated value of g, and give answers to an accuracy that suits it.

skills.title: Use F = μR
skills.description: Use F = μR when sliding or in limiting equilibrium, after finding R by resolving.

skills.title: Limiting equilibrium and F ≤ μR
skills.description: Use F ≤ μR in equilibrium, and F = μR when on the point of slipping, to find μ or a force.

skills.title: Direction of friction
skills.description: Decide which way friction acts by working out which way the body would tend to move.

skills.title: Decide whether a body moves
skills.description: Compare the force trying to cause motion with maximum friction μR to decide whether the body stays at rest.

skills.title: Take moments about a point
skills.description: Form a moments equation using force × perpendicular distance, choosing a point that removes unknown forces.

skills.title: Moments of forces at an angle
skills.description: Find perpendicular distances (or components) with sin and cos when the rod or force is inclined.

skills.title: Reactions at smooth contacts
skills.description: Know that a smooth wall, peg, rail or drum gives a reaction perpendicular to the surface or rod.

skills.title: Combine resolving and moments
skills.description: Use moments with resolving in two directions to find all unknown forces on a rigid body in equilibrium.

skills.title: Positions allowed by a force limit
skills.description: Set up and solve an inequality (for example tension ≤ maximum) to find where a load can be placed.

skills.title: Effect of moving the centre of mass
skills.description: Explain how a non-uniform rod, with its centre of mass closer to one end, changes the moments and reactions.

skills.title: Mechanics modelling assumptions
skills.description: Explain the meaning and effect of the model terms particle, light, inextensible, smooth, uniform and rough.

skills.title: Refine a mechanics model
